main_issue: Who gets to use the single window corner of the living room (shrine, desk, laundry, or friends' seating), with no agreed resolution.

A-B.evidence: B asks A about alternatives (25) and A refuses (26); B's turn 4 claim for friends conflicts with A, but B moves to neutral mediation (8, 30), with no agreement reached.

A-C.evidence: Both insist their use is essential (3, 5, 9, 17, 26), with no direct exchange; they are mildly sympathetic via A's turn 7 "we all use this corner".

A-D.evidence: A says 'I understand it's for prayers' but still holds the corner for work (7); D says 'I'm the only one who gets no space' (28); both hold to their claims.

B-C.evidence: B accepts 'the laundry has to be there' (22) after C's explanations (21), but B's turn 30 says nobody should claim it permanently.

B-D.evidence: B probes D's alternatives (22), D says there's no other space (24); B replies to D's complaint with 'That's not it' (30) and frames it as shared loss.

C-D.evidence: D: 'You can't have a shrine next to drying laundry' (10); C: 'there is no other place with a window' (13); D complains about unequal treatment (14); no concession.
